title: Fast Matrix Multiplication · Strassen / AlphaTensor Frontier
tagline: Exact bilinear rank over the integers and GF(2)
question: How few scalar products suffice to multiply two small matrices exactly?
description: Prove Strassen’s seven-product construction and the tensor-product composition rule. Then certify smaller integer schemes for 3×3 by 3×4 and 3×4 by 4×5, or improve on AlphaTensor’s 47 products for 4×4 over GF(2).
verdict: Open for integer and GF(2) rank certificates.

impact.ships_to: BLIS / OpenBLAS, CUTLASS / Triton GEMM, GF(2) crypto & erasure coding, NumPy/SciPy
impact.bottleneck: General matrix multiplication (GEMM) dominates AI training, scientific simulation, and signal processing. Practical fast matmul is gated not just by scalar product count (rank) but by addition count and unit {-1,0,1} coefficients that preserve FP16/BF16 numerical stability.
impact.what_one_step_buys: Cutting 1 scalar multiplication in a 3×3×3 or 4×4×4 base kernel compounds exponentially across recursive block levels (r^L vs 27^L); shaving additions with {-1,0,1} coefficients directly lowers the crossover matrix size where fast GEMM beats schoolbook in real BLAS libraries.

consumers.name: BLIS / Fast-Strassen GEMM
consumers.detail: Fused 1–2 level Strassen and rectangular (3×3×4, 3×4×5) microkernels reduce FLOPs on large dense matrices.

consumers.name: M4RI / GF(2) Linear Algebra & PQC
consumers.detail: AlphaTensor's 47-product 4×4 GF(2) scheme directly accelerates binary matrix multiplication in coding theory and post-quantum crypto.

consumers.name: FMM Catalog (Univ. Lille / AlphaTensor)
consumers.detail: Authoritative database of exact bilinear algorithms with machine-checked certificates.

examples.mechanism: Unit {-1, 0, 1} coefficients avoid rescaling multipliers and keep rounding error bounded; minimizing additions lowers the crossover threshold in BLAS/GPU kernels.
examples.metric: Standard Laderman uses 98 additions; sparse unit-coeff schemes cut additions by >30% at the same 23 products.

examples.mechanism: Any 22-product integer scheme composes via MM-003 into O(N^{log_3 22}) = O(N^{2.813}) exact matrix multiplication over every ring.
examples.metric: Beating 23 products over ℤ would break Laderman's 1976 record (proven LB = 19).

examples.use_case: Fast GF(2) matrix engines & binary erasure coding
examples.mechanism: Every verified SchemeF2 4 4 4 compiles straight to bitwise XOR/AND block operations for M4RI and binary ECC decoders.
examples.metric: 47 products beats two-level Strassen (49) by 4.1% per recursion level; 46 sets a new world record.

objectives.title: Match the published product counts

objectives.title: Laderman 3×3×3 Frontier & Hardware-Friendly Addition Minimization
